```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

`geo_chat()` connects GEO metadata tables to a large language model (LLM) so
that you can explore them with natural language: *find single-cell studies
with more than 20 samples*, *which platforms dominate these datasets?*, or
*filter to post-2020 human studies*. Under the hood it delegates schema
summarization, SQL querying, and dashboard filtering to the
[querychat](https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/r/) package, so the model
never needs the raw table serialized into the prompt — it queries your local
copy with SQL instead.

Three functions cover the whole workflow:

- `geo_chat()` creates and returns a `QueryChat` object
- `geo_shiny()` creates it and immediately launches a Shiny app
- `geo_console()` creates it and immediately starts a console chat

```{r setup}
library(geokit)
```

## Prerequisites

1. Install [querychat](https://posit-dev.github.io/querychat/r/) if it is not
   already on your system. It is currently archived on CRAN, so install it
   from the posit-dev R-universe:

   ```r
   install.packages(
     "querychat",
     repos = c("https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos"))
   )
   ```

2. To chat with a plain data frame, querychat needs a local SQL engine:
   install either `duckdb` or `RSQLite`.
3. Configure an LLM client (see the next section).

> **Note**: LLM answers are generated from your metadata by an external
> model, so treat them as suggestions and verify important selections
> yourself.

## Choosing an LLM Client

The first argument of `geo_chat()`, `client`, is passed to querychat and
accepts:

- `NULL` (default): querychat uses the `querychat.client` option, the
  `QUERYCHAT_CLIENT` environment variable, or falls back to
  `ellmer::chat_openai()`.
- An [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/) `Chat` object, for full control
  over model, base URL, and system prompt:

  ```r
  client <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-4o-mini")
  ```

- A provider string understood by `ellmer::chat()`, such as
  `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"`.
- A function returning a `Chat` object — handy for OpenAI-compatible
  endpoints or custom credentials. querychat calls the function with
  `system_prompt = NULL`:

  ```r
  client <- \(system_prompt = NULL) ellmer::chat_openai_compatible(
    base_url = "https://example.com/v1",
    model = "my-model",
    api_key = Sys.getenv("MY_API_KEY"),
    system_prompt = system_prompt
  )
  ```

API keys are read from environment variables by ellmer (e.g.,
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); set them in your `.Renviron`.

## From Search Results to a Chat Session

A typical session starts with `geo_search()`. The returned data frame can be
handed to `geo_chat()` directly:

```{r chat-from-search, eval = FALSE}
records <- geo_search(
  "diabetes[ALL] AND Homo sapiens[ORGN] AND GSE[ETYP]"
)

chat <- geo_chat(
  NULL,
  records,
  data_description = paste(
    "GEO DataSets records about diabetes in human, one row per record.",
    "The Contains column lists related GSM/GSE/GPL accessions."
  )
)
```

`data_description` gives the model background about what the columns mean,
which noticeably improves query quality. Use `extra_instructions` for
additional behavioral rules (both are passed through to querychat).

## From a Metadata Database to a Chat Session

For richer series-level metadata, build a local database with `geo_meta()`
first (see `vignette("geometadb")`) and chat with that table:

```{r chat-from-meta, eval = FALSE}
meta <- geo_meta(
  records[["Series Accession"]][1:20],
  odir = tempdir()
)

qc <- geo_chat(
  NULL,
  meta,
  data_description = paste(
    "One row per GEO Series fetched from SOFT metadata.",
    "Series_title, Series_summary and Series_overall_design describe each",
    "study; Series_sample_id lists its GSM accessions separated by '; '."
  )
)
```

The object returned by `geo_chat()` is a standard `QueryChat` object, so you
can launch the interface whenever you are ready:

```{r launch, eval = FALSE}
qc$app() # or qc$console() for the terminal
```

The convenience wrappers do both steps at once:

```{r wrappers, eval = FALSE}
geo_shiny(NULL, records) # build + launch Shiny app
geo_console(NULL, records) # build + start console chat
```

## A Self-Contained Example

The following example needs no LLM access — it only builds and destroys the
chat object, which is useful to verify your installation:

```{r demo-object, eval = rlang::is_installed("querychat") && (rlang::is_installed("duckdb") || rlang::is_installed("RSQLite"))}
records <- data.frame(
  `Series Accession` = c("GSE1", "GSE2"),
  Title = c("human diabetes study", "mouse liver study"),
  Type = c("Expression profiling by array", "RNA-seq"),
  Samples = c(12L, 8L),
  check.names = FALSE
)

chat <- geo_chat(NULL, records, cleanup = TRUE)
chat$cleanup()
```
